name: The Meeting Place Cannot Be Changed
description: The main road in Bytecity is a straight line from south to north. Conveniently, there are coordinates measured in meters from the southernmost building in north direction. At some points on the road there are n friends, and i -th of them is standing at the point x i meters and can move with any speed no greater than v i meters per second in any of the two directions along the road: south or north. You are to compute the minimum time needed to gather all the n friends at some point on the road. Note that the point they meet at doesn't need to have integer coordinate.
input_specification: The first line contains single integer n ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 60 000 ) — the number of friends. The second line contains n integers x 1 , x 2 , ..., x n ( 1 ≤ x i ≤ 10 9 ) — the current coordinates of the friends, in meters. The third line contains n integers v 1 , v 2 , ..., v n ( 1 ≤ v i ≤ 10 9 ) — the maximum speeds of the friends, in meters per second.
output_specification: Print the minimum time (in seconds) needed for all the n friends to meet at some point on the road. Your answer will be considered correct, if its absolute or relative error isn't greater than 10 - 6 . Formally, let your answer be a , while jury's answer be b . Your answer will be considered correct if holds.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 780B — The Meeting Place Cannot Be Changed [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
